review: 1:3 בִּרְצוֹן־לֵב שָׁלֵם — 'with the full will of the heart', for بِالرِّضَا التَّامّ (complete consent); the phrase keeps the voluntariness of the cross.
2:1 כַּשֶּׂה הוּבַל לַטֶּבַח — Isaiah 53:7 (כַּשֶּׂה לַטֶּבַח יוּבָל); the verse is quoted rather than translated.
2:3 בֶּן־עֶלְיוֹן — 'Son of the Most High' (Luke 1:32); the Arabic ابْنُ الْعَلِيّ means the same, and the Hebrew title is fixed.
3:1 הַצּוֹרֵר — 'the adversary'; the biblical noun is צַר/צוֹרֵר (Esth 3:10), chosen over שָׂטָן because the verse is about the enemy's apparent victory, not about naming him.
5:1 בַּמָּוֶת הֵמִית מָוֶת — 'by death He put death to death'; the paronomasia of the Arabic (أَبْطَلَ الْمَوْتَ بِالْمَوْتِ) is kept with the same root repeated.
6:2 הַלֵּל וְכָבוֹד רַב — 'praise and great honour'; the Arabic has three nouns (thanks, praise, honour), Hebrew folds two of them into this line to keep the 66.86 shape.
